notes.title: Season 2 Preview Patch Highlights!
notes.notes:
Season 2 will begin on October 18th, but the official "preview" patch has arrived which includes many of the new changes for season 2. Here is a brief summary of the new highlights:


 Runes now drop! Runes may be added to items with open sockets which will permanently modify the item's properties. Each rune provides different properties, and some runes are extremely valuable due to their rarity!
 Many items, of all rarity types, may have sockets. Each socket allows for a rune to be added to the item. Runes cannot be removed from an item.
 A new ethereal property may appear on all items except for jewelry (rings, amulets, and charms). This property may appear for all rarity types. It will boost the base armor or damage for the armor or weapon, respectively. The only catch is that the item will degrade over time. After the ethereal item drops to 0 durability, the item will be destroyed.
 A new Indestructible property now appears on some items. This is a very valuable property in cases where the item is also ethereal because it prevents the item from decaying. A very rare rune can even add the indestructible property to an item!
 Runes may be found randomly from mobs and chests. However they are also awarded as part of the King's Reward upon completing each difficulty. Note that the King's Reward drops with a special modifier that increases the odds of finding the rarest runes in the game!
 A new global General chat channel is now used in favor of relying on "town" channels. Players no longer default to numbered town channels. Instead they default to a private channel although players may still manually join any channel. The matchmaking and global chat system has made the need for local presence detection in town obsolete.


[previewyoutube=Jokmcrrew7U;full][/previewyoutube]

Note that runes and socketed items drop, however you will not be able to access the crafting counter until the start of season 2! In the meantime, we will monitor rune drop rates and consider the need for adjustments before the new season begins!

And one final nugget of news is that we plan on adding support for traditional Chinese. We hope that this will be patched before October! The game has received quite a bit of support in Taiwan and Malaysia in recent weeks, so we plan to provide an ideal translation for those players!

See you on October 18th!

notes.title: Nevergrind Online - Full Release Trailer & Season 1 Announcement
notes.notes:
Official Launch

Season 1 of Nevergrind Online officially begins on July 11th, 2024! Steam's first multiplayer blobber first released back on June 9th, 2022. Since that time, development has continued at a steady pace which helped pave the way for its release! Check out the Full Release Official Trailer below! We just updated Nevergrind Online store page with fresh screenshots and the latest trailer, so feel welcome to check that out too!

[previewyoutube=EPbJsPhueNQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Future Development

Expect development to continue after season 1 begins. We still have a list of features on our roadmap which would be great additions to the game. Originally, we planned to finish everything, but we also want to avoid keeping the game in Early Access for too long. At this time, we believe that the most critical gameplay features have been completed and that now would be a good time for full release. 

There are many features that we would love to add including an auction house, a crafting system, and a mercenary system. We also have many other ideas up our sleeve to help make Nevergrind Online the ultimate cooperative dungeon crawling experience!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37895771/3820c48b3a9c991b13205549c3745f8679924bae.jpg

Season 1 FAQ

For early access players, note that your banked Ladder items will NOT transfer to your Eternal bank. Again, banked Ladder items do NOT transfer! If you have special items on Ladder that you want to keep, you must equip them or put them in a character's inventory. All Ladder characters and their items will transfer to the Eternal realm at the start of Season 1. Since all characters are moved to the Eternal realm, the Ladder's leaderboard will completely reset and the economy will start fresh.

notes.title: Taunt improvements, bug fixes, difficulty tuning
notes.notes:
283: Early Access 0.13.22 - August 27, 2022 2:35 PM EST
• Taunt now locks the target to you for a minimum fixed duration.
• Shield Bash (WAR) no longer has a cooldown.
• Zealous Slam (CRU) and Shield Break (SHD) now taunt their targets.
• Fixed a bug that allowed for heal messages to display and buffs to apply to slain targets.
• Mime Strike will now work on all three Hurricane Kicks (MNK).
• Fixed a bug that allowed certain properties to incorrectly appear on certain rare items, such as Two-hand Blunt on shields.
• Champion mobs are now more common on nightmare and hell difficulty. They are the most common in hell.
• Adjusted how many mobs could be champ/uniques before level 20. You won't see more than one per battle below level 10. You won't see more than two before level 20. The maximum total of champ/uniques has also been lowered.
• Fixed the layout of the leaderboard now that experience values are longer.
• The experience penalty for playing in nightmare mode has been increased from 77 to 79.
• Health, mana, and spirit recovery properties are now more powerful in nightmare and hell. Previously the leech, wraith rates in higher difficulties were much lower.

notes.title: Bug fixes and difficulty adjustments
notes.notes:

• Fixed the store reset bug. Also increased the store reset interval. 😊
• The character stat tab now display casting haste% and faster cast rate as separate fields to help avoid confusion. Faster cast rate is more like a rating that increases spellcasting speed, not a raw percentage boost. I hope that helps clear up the confusion!
• Boosted the natural armor of mobs in nightmare and hell.
• Adjusted melee miss rates and hit% cap slightly.
• Exp find has been removed from rare items. It will still appear on some unique, set items.
• Reduced mob resists in nightmare and hell.

259: Early Access 0.12.96 - August 3, 2022 11:10 PM EST
• Made some critical improvements. ☺

• Fixed Tornado's (DRU) indicated ice damage on its tooltip.
• Fixed a bug related to how Gravity Flux sometimes removes Stasis Field (ENC) from the wrong target when you slay a mob.
• The trade window's gold input now only accepts integers. It will also validate the gold value as you type it in case it exceeds your current gold (or other limits). Overall the gold input works much better and provides better feedback.

notes.title: Party bug fixes, base stat improvements, bard improvements
notes.notes:
253: Early Access 0.12.90 - July 31, 2022 12:35 PM EST
• Fixed all of the annoying party bugs related to invite, disband, leader election.
• Blessed Hammer (CRU) no longer cancels when your target dies.
• Litany of Life (BRD) is now considered a HoT rather than a buff to health regen. This means that they will now show up in healing reports.
• Litany of Life and Melody of Mana (BRD) can now benefit from arcane magic bonuses, alteration, and charisma. The new values are reflected in the skill tooltips as well.
• Your leader's ability to invite is no longer constrained by players that joined your party.
• Improved /who lfg level filtering. There were some bugs with it.
• Strength now has a more noticeable impact on melee damage.
• Dexterity now has a more powerful impact on critical hit rates.
• Agility now has a bigger impact on armor which helps with damage reduction.
• Wisdom, intelligence, and charisma now have a more noticeable impact on spell damage based on school magic type (evocation, alteration, and conjuration).
• Mob health has been increased slightly to account for these improvements to hero base attributes.
• Corrected some in-game text about piercing vs penetrating skills.

notes.title: All Shards Re-Merged (AGAIN). 🤞 Plus Bug Fixes.
notes.notes:
244: Early Access 0.12.81 - July 26, 2022 4:00 PM EST
• Invested a ton of time and energy upgrading the server architecture to support one large online world. This is attempt #2 to get rid of sharding.
• Fixed a bug that was preventing add elemental damage and passive skills from properly rolling on rare items.
• You can no longer trade while in combat. This just seemed annoying and pointless to me. You can still trade in town, empty rooms, or in dungeon hallways.
• Removed Prowl's (ROG) movement debuff (hehe).
• Condemnation (CLR) now staggers its targets as intended.
• You can now identify equipped items in the rare case where your equipment somehow becomes unidentified. This is very rare and it's not the right solution, but it does enable the player to fix their bugged state.
• Improved session handling to prevent bugs that make it appear like you logged out.
• Updated Japanese localization!
• The average ping indicator now indicates your average ping over the last minute. Previously, it averaged across a longer period of time. A minute is probably a better range of time.
• A mechanism is now in place to prevent mass spamming of party invites. This will help prevent party bugs and persuade party leaders to be more selective with their invites. Note that their party lockout is quite brief, so it is not a big deal. The idea is to prevent a party of four from inviting ten people. Instead, just find one person that actually wants to join.
• Probably fixed the combat music not playing in a hallway battle bug.

notes.title: All Monster Animations Re-mastered and Ready for Final Release!
notes.notes:
Since I started development back in 2017, a lot has changed since I originally created the mob animations. Each monster used a fixed number of frames. I settled on 105 frames to cover all of the attacks, hit, special, and death animations needed for Nevergrind Online. At the time, I felt that I had to really limit the number of frames due to memory-related concerns. In the process of capturing the 2D frames, I had to leave out many of the frames used in the game. This is particularly noticeable on larger monsters that make fast lateral movements.

After several iterations to improve compression and performance, I realized that I could easily improve the animations and drop the 105-frame limitation. Instead I could just capture the entire animation without dropping a single frame! I knew it would be a fair amount of work, but it was certainly worth it!

Check out the video below which shows the difference between early iterations and the modern version!

[previewyoutube=YJ-BijHxC0E;full][/previewyoutube]

We are ironing out minor small bugs and preparing our servers for release in June! We don't have a hard date yet, but it will be released in June for certain. The 10th, 17th, or 24th are the most likely dates. I am going to work on updating the store page's screenshots and record a trailer for release since there have been so many changes since I last updated them! This is a unique type of dungeon crawl "blobber", so the trailer will try to do a good job explaining what makes Nevergrind Online special and very different from other dungeon crawlers out there.

notes.title: Remastering All Animations for Final Release!
notes.notes:
Before the game is ready for release, I knew that I had to remaster the animations! In the course of development, I have discovered numerous techniques that help optimize the performance of the animations. Those optimizations have enabled us to use much more fluid animation, more frames per model, and a more flexible animation model.

Check out the video below for a sneak peak at how fluid animation will look in the final release!

[previewyoutube=4EEC7btmcME;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Nevergrind Online Looks Promising for June Release!
notes.notes:
State of the Game

Nevergrind Online is in good shape for a June release! We have been working hard since July 2020 when our alpha phase started! Thanks to the hundreds of eager testers that have helped NGO become what it is, today! There have been countless enhancements, suggestions, and bugs that have been resolved thanks to their stalwart efforts! 

Here's a brief milestone overview of features that have been enhanced or completed since the alpha began:
General
✅Single player mode completed.
✅Added a heroic mode to challenge full parties of adventurers.
✅Completed writing the lore for all missions.
✅Sprinkled boss encounters throughout the story mode.
✅Mission quest mobs now have specific drop types.
✅Added a victory screen and King reward to the game.
✅Optimized all images to a very efficient image format.
✅Finished the tavern tips and loading screen tips.
✅Finalized the sound effects.
✅Completed the advanced statistics tab on the character sheet.
✅Added support for 4k monitors.
✅Added a patch history tool within the game.
✅Added a call-to-action prompt that guides the user to certain actions throughout the game.

Creation
✅12 playable races.
✅14 playable classes.
✅Enabled artflow.ai avatars for future unlimited avatar possibilities.
✅Support for 16 avatars per race and 64 avatars for humans.

Town 
✅Fully animated town including alternate artwork for four times of day, morning, afternoon, evening, and night.
✅Guild functionality completed.
✅Tavern functionality completed.
✅Apothecary functionality completed.
✅Blacksmith functionality completed.
✅Academy functionality completed.
✅Merchant functionality completed.
✅Bank functionality completed.

Dungeon
✅Completed procedural map generation for 14 different zones.
✅Eliminated party follower map position bugs.
✅Fixed graphical glitches while navigating through dungeons.

Combat
✅Finished class-based adjustments of all skills.
✅Some weapons now have proc effects.
✅Mobs now have a secondary attack cycle that enables them to use certain special skills in addition to their main attack cycle based on their class.
✅Added several new monster champion traits.
✅Added fully integrated DPS meters in the game.

Itemization
✅Unique items have been completed.
✅Set items and their according bonuses have been completed.
✅Chests can now drop potions and scrolls.

What's Left?
At this point, I am focused on optimizations, enhancements, adjustments, and other minor features. The game is very playable and I am doing everything possible to ensure an enjoyable gaming experience for groups of adventurers at launch! Wishlist the game and I'll see you in June!

notes.title: Patch update 133
notes.notes:
Mob trait rampage is now slightly more delayed to give players a chance to react or counter the flurry of attacks.
 The number of swings rampage triggers is now limited by mob level. A level 8 mob will swing three times. A level 40 mob will swing seven times. Seven is the max.
 Reduced Blizzard cast time from 5 to 4.5 seconds.
 MANY spells which previously canceled casting if your target died will now allow you to continue casting. This was particularly adjusted for spells that hit multiple targets. For example, maybe your target died while casting Blizzard, but that's okay! You continue casting and hit the AE targets anyway.
 Changed Centurion Shiloh's trait from bloodlusted to spirit drain.
 Changed Salubrin Haven's quests from 2/4/6/8 to 1/3/5/7. This gives new players more control over what type of mobs they'll face in the early missions.
 Fixed a bug that was causing paralyze to not apply properly by some attacks such as Monk's Palm Strike.
